page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.4xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an ARMv9-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, but includes a baseline network bandwidth of 33 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory subsystem performance, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top tier. Large block read-only memory bandwidth reaches 297.05 GB/sec, and large block write memory bandwidth is measured at 137.97 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Passmark database operations also demonstrate strong performance, while CPU-bound tasks such as stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores fall within the average range.

The server exhibits performance tradeoffs in machine learning tasks, with weak to poor results in large language model inference, particularly for text generation on larger models. Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong database benchmark results, this instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and caching layers like Redis, rather than heavy parallel computing or AI inference.
